title: Nvidia commits up to $3B for a 20% stake in Stargate's power partner Lancium at a $10B valuation
subtitle: The chipmaker takes an equity position in the Blackstone-backed developer that owns the 1,000-acre Abilene campus anchoring OpenAI–SoftBank–Oracle's Stargate program.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Nvidia agreed to invest up to $3 billion in Lancium, the Blackstone-backed power-infrastructure developer behind Stargate's Abilene, Texas site, according to reporting by The Information carried by Bloomberg and Yahoo on August 10. The structure: $2 billion up front for roughly a 20% stake at a ~$10B valuation, with another $1B contingent on Lancium hitting milestones including new grid hookups. Lancium owns the 1,000-acre Lancium Clean Campus that serves as Stargate's first operational site and is reportedly weighing a 2027 public listing.

This is the same story as this week's Anthropic–Macquarie–GIC Theseus JV, told from Nvidia's angle. Selling GPUs is no longer the constraint; getting them plugged in is. Every hyperscaler and frontier lab is now competing for grid interconnects on timelines the utilities can't meet, and the fastest path to more sockets is capital in the developers who own the land, the substation queue positions, and the offtake contracts. Nvidia investing directly in Lancium is a vertical-integration move — protecting its own volume by owning a slice of the choke point.

The deal also tightens a knot that has been forming for a year: Stargate is nominally a SoftBank–OpenAI–Oracle venture, but its power partner is Blackstone-backed Lancium, its chips come from Nvidia, and increasingly its financing comes from a stack of infrastructure investors rather than the operating companies' balance sheets. Add Anthropic's Theseus this week, Broadcom's role in the 150B Google-Anthropic financing on August 5, and TSMC's record capex, and a picture emerges: AI is being financed like a utility buildout, with private-credit and infrastructure capital carrying most of the load.

For learners: read the money, not the model names. When a chipmaker invests in a power company, when a frontier lab spins up a data-center JV with an asset manager, when a $500B Stargate becomes a stack of overlapping equity and lease agreements, those signals tell you what the industry actually believes about the next five years. Understanding the plumbing — grid interconnect timelines, PPAs, colocation contracts, offtake economics — is a genuinely differentiated skill for anyone entering AI right now.
